title: capacity-scrub-and-edge-anomaly-capture-2029-08-05
content:
Purpose:
Notes from the capacity scrub + edge anomaly capture session (weekly infrastructure update). Focus: identify transient capacity sinks in APAC-edge, reconcile reserve pools, and set short-term mitigations for customer impacting throttles.

High-level summary:
- Observed a pattern of short-lived GPU slot shortages in SEA edge region (edge-03) over the last 72 hours causing increased queuing and elevated latency spikes for tail traffic (p99 token latency jump from 220ms -> 410ms during 03:00-05:00 UTC).
- Root-cause hypothesis: overlap of nightly maintenance jobs + a new autoscaler scoring edge case that double-counts pre-pulled warm instances for burst pools (see JIRA-ENG-1142).
- Immediate mitigations applied: temp disable of noncritical prewarm jobs, tightened autoscaler cooldown for edge-03, bumped spare pool from 6 -> 10 GPUs for the next 48 hours.

What we checked (data sources):
- Scheduler metrics (slot-alloc-rate, prewarm-signal) across edge regions: engine-metrics cluster, 2029-08-02 -> 2029-08-05.
- Node health logs from edge-03 (kubelet restarts, OOMs) via SRE-logs. No sustained node OOMs found during spike windows.
- Telemetry: per-customer queue length and prioritization traces for customers on Dedicated pools (customer A & B showed queue dwell > 10s).
- Autoscaler traces (scoring function) and rollout notes from last deploy (deploy-2029-07-30).

Detailed findings:
1) Autoscaler scoring duplication: The new prewarm-count metric introduced in the July rollout is being aggregated twice for burst-eligible pools when both 'implicit' and 'explicit' prewarm configs are present. This doubles the effective prewarm footprint reported to the scheduler and causes the autoscaler to underprovision live pools in some windows. Repro steps recorded in JIRA-ENG-1142.
2) Maintenance job collision: An internal nightly maintenance job that runs image cleanup and disk trimming (maintenance-images-v2) begins sweeping at 02:50 UTC in several APAC-edge clusters; when combined with short windows of API-driven cold-starts, this can transiently reduce available slots during the 03:00-04:30 UTC period.
3) Warm pool depletion pattern: Some newer fleets (v2 hardware profile) were not correctly inheriting the spare-pool reservation policy; they started joining the general allocation pool, increasing contention for customer-facing slots.

Customer impact & incidents:
- No SEV declared. Impacted tail latency for a subset of Dedicated customers during nightly hours (repeated intermittent throttles). That surfaced as increased retry rates in customer instrumentation and a handful of support tickets. CS informed and proactive messages sent.

Decisions made in the meeting:
- Roll back the prewarm-count aggregation change (hotfix) to avoid double-counting. Owner: Marco. Target: 2029-08-06 12:00 UTC (hotfix branch + canary in staging).
- Disable maintenance-images-v2 sweeping on edge-03 and edge-05 for a 72-hour window while we validate image cleanup alternatives. Owner: Lena. Target: 2029-08-06 02:00 UTC.
- Enforce spare-pool reservation policy at fleet creation via admission controller check (short-term policy enforcement script). Owner: Daniel. Target: 2029-08-07 EOD.
- Increase short-term spare buffer for APAC-edge from 6 -> 10 GPUs (already applied). Owner: Priya (oncall). Monitoring: auto roll-back if CPU/GPU utilization > 85% for more than 4 hours.

Action items & owners:
- Marco Ruiz: create hotfix PR for autoscaler aggregation edge case. Link PR to JIRA-ENG-1142. (ETA 2029-08-06 12:00 UTC).
- Lena Zhou: schedule maintenance job pause and produce alternative cleanup plan that runs during low-traffic windows; include cost delta estimate. (ETA 2029-08-08).
- Daniel Kim: implement admission-controller check to validate spare-pool inheritance on new fleets and backfill existing fleets via a one-off job. (ETA 2029-08-07).
- Priya Menon: monitor spare-pool buffer effects and report if customer tail latencies return to baseline; escalate to SRE if anomalies persist. (Ongoing; update in next weekly).
- SRE rotation: pay attention to edge-03 02:30-05:30 UTC window for the next 5 days; use the temporary debug flags enabled for deeper traces (debug flag x-edge-debug = true).

Follow-ups (broader):
- Medium term (2–4 weeks): Add a dedicated 'nightly-maintenance' simulation to the capacity lab so we can reproduce maintenance + burst patterns. Owner: capacity-tools.
- Longer term (quarter): Rework autoscaler to decouple prewarm accounting from live allocation signals; aim for clearer invariants and unit tests. Owner: autoscaler team; ticket: ENG-AUTO-337.

Notes to self / open questions:
- Is there any customer using custom prewarm knobs that we haven't accounted for? Quick audit of customer config store recommended.
- Verify that the admission-controller won't cause churn for legacy fleet creation automation (we need a safe rollout path).

Meeting attendees (live + dial-in):
- Aisha Patel (notes)
additional_notes: Quick log captures attached in Confluence link in linked_artifacts; CS ticket summary: CS-5992 and CS-5996. We'll reassess spare buffer on 2029-08-08 and decide on permanent reserve sizing after 48h telemetry.
